Main topics: recent kernel upgrade regression on p95 tail, egress routing fallbacks, telemetry gaps (lack of token-level cost in private infra), and runbook for automated model fallback. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tomás (Redwood SE), Hannah (CSM), Eli (Infra), Alex (CTO - Greenwave), Priya (Platform), Jordan (Security), Samir (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um, quick check — Jordan, Priya, Alex, can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Jordan: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:10] Alex: yep good here. running a little late this morning so appreciate the sync.
[00:20] Maya: cool, agenda: 1) telemetry gaps we saw after the kernel bump, 2) fallback / routing playbook, 3) next steps & extended perf test. Tomás will walk recent perf numbers.
[00:35] Tomás: ok so quick recap — we rolled the 1.4.2 kernel yesterday on the dev cluster. overall throughput looks fine but p95 spiked about 2.1x on a subset of requests, specifically the long-seq chat flows where KV lookups are frequent. p50 stayed around 130ms, p95 moved from 380ms to ~820ms for that cohort.
[01:02] Priya: that matches what Samir saw in prod-ish env, we had a couple of user flows timeout at 10s which is bad.
[01:10] Samir: yeah, timeouts only on requests that hit the external embeddings service then waited on egress routing — some of our routes went to CloudVendorX as part of the fallback chain and that added unexpected latency.
[01:25] Tomás: hmm, interesting — our routing policy currently tries local on‑prem -> region fallback -> vendor fallback. We saw a pathological path where prefix cache wasn't warmed so the model did more KV fetches and triggered an egress to the embeddings endpoint. there may be a serialization/lock contention in the 1.4.2 GPU kernel that surfaces with concurrent KV hits.
[01:55] Eli: is that the same kay-vee cache you mean? it's often transcribed as kay-vee in the logs so that's why our dashboards miss some of the hits.
[02:08] Tomás: yeah, logs show 'kv_cache_hits' but some collectors drop the metric when using the newer runtime. that's a telemetry gap.
[02:20] Hannah: to be explicit, telemetry gaps are: token-level cost not reported in private infra, intermittent kv cache hit metrics missing, and no per-request route-level trace in the console for private deployments.
[02:35] Jordan: security note — the KMS key rotation job failed once after the upgrade and we had to rekey a test container. not a blocker but needs documenting; also we need to confirm whether Redwood's private control plane will store audit logs in our S3 or push to our SIEM, that impacts our retention policy.
[02:55] Maya: thanks. quick thought on fallback playbook: we should have an ordered set: 1) detect p95 > threshold, 2) check kv cache hit rate, 3) if hit rate < X then route traffic to larger model with warmed cache in dedicated pool, 4) if dedicated not available fallback to hosted Redwood API with data egress allowed (with DLP on). we drafted a playbook already.
[03:28] Alex: question — sending to hosted Redwood API triggers data residency concerns; Jordan will only accept that if payloads are redacted or if we use tokenization.
[03:40] Jordan: right, we need a legal signoff, but for emergency failover we can allow minimal fields out — per our policy.
[03:47] Tomás: we can add a transform that strips PHI before egress and still keeps context, we demoed a similar redact pipeline in last year's POC.
[03:58] Priya: okay good. on telemetry, is there a way to get token-level cost breakdown in our private observability? we only see aggregate GPU-hours right now.
[04:12] Eli: current private agent reports tokens_per_request as a metric but we haven't integrated token-to-cost mapping because prices vary by model and we wanted Redwood's cost mapping to be pushed as a separate dataset.
[04:24] Maya: action item for us: Tomás to produce an exporter that maps model/token counts -> estimated cost using the pilot's chosen model config, so Greenwave can see burn per-route.
[04:36] Tomás: yes, I'll prototype that. it will be best-effort and flagged experimental.
[04:44] Samir: quick note, on the egress side the firewall team added a transient rule that reroutes to CloudVendorX for specific endpoints during the weekend; we didn't realize fallback logic would hit those endpoints and cause the extra hop. please add that to the playbook as a config check.
[04:59] Maya: good catch. we'll add a checklist: firewall egress rules, KMS access, SIEM sinks, and canary percentage.
[05:10] Tomás: going back to perf numbers — for the extended test we'd like to run with two variants: A) batch_size=4, prefix cache warmup, and B) batch_size=8 with the same warmup. We'll also toggle the kernel path (1.4.1 vs 1.4.2) to see regression delta. Expected result: if 1.4.2 has a kernel contention bug, variant B might amplify it.
[05:40] Priya: how long do you need?
[05:42] Tomás: 48 hours per variant to get stable p95 tails, so about 4 days total but we can run both concurrently if you have two dev clusters.
[05:52] Priya: we have one dev cluster and one staging; we can run them concurrently. Samir will allocate.
[05:58] Samir: yes I can schedule staging for variant B tomorrow.
[06:03] Jordan: one more security ask — when we route to hosted for fallback, we want a signed consent toggle in the console and an audit entry for each failover. can Redwood's control plane surface that?
[06:15] Hannah: we have an audit hook that can forward entries to your SIEM. the consent toggle is an interesting product ask; we can add a manual approval step in the canary playbook for now.
[06:28] Alex: will that manual step block automated recovery? we want automated recovery in high-severity incidents.
[06:34] Maya: suggestion: for P0 incidents allow auto-fallback to hosted with redaction; for P1/P2 require manual approval. add to playbook.
[06:44] Alex: ok agreed.
[06:46] Tomás: small note about telemetry collection — collectors that use filebeat had a config mismatch after the upgrade which caused some metrics to be written under 'runtime.v2' instead of 'runtime.v1', so dashboards didn't pick them up. we'll provide a migration mapping.
[07:05] Eli: we'll patch filebeat and backfill missing metrics for the 24h window.
[07:10] Priya: can you also add a metric for 'route_miss_reason' so we can see why a request fell back? e.g., capacity|cache_miss|timeout|security_block.
[07:21] Tomás: yes, we can add route_miss_reason as a tag on traces.
[07:28] Maya: ok we're nearing time — recap and owners: Tomás does the 48h head-to-head + cost exporter; Maya sends fallback playbook + checklist; Jordan shares KMS & retention; Priya provides traffic profile; Samir schedules staging run.
[07:47] Alex: thanks all. can you also include the benchmark CSV and a heatmap? the spreadsheet link was shared in the chat.
[07:56] Maya: yes, links in the notes — see shared_artifacts.
[08:01] Jordan: one last thing: competitor note — MegaCorp AI had an outage last week and their fallbacks sent customers to a hosted partner which caused a data leakage scare; just flagging that we don't want a similar chain.
[08:18] Maya: good caution. we'll add a dependency matrix to the playbook that shows which fallback targets we trust and legal constraints for each.
[08:30] Closing: next sync same time next week unless the 48h run surfaces blockers; we'll reconvene earlier if needed.

End transcript.

Recap (auto):
- Root cause hypothesis: 1.4.2 kernel contention + prefix cache warmup issues causing p95 spike.
- Telemetry gaps: token-level cost mapping, dropped kv_cache metrics, route-level traces.
- Actions: extended perf tests, exporter for cost estimates, fallback playbook update, KMS confirmation.
notes: Transcription contains a few ASR artifacts (kay-vee -> KV, filebeat names) — verify metric names before automated dashboards.
